The present claim petition for compensation relates to grievous injuries suffered by the petitioner in a road accident that took place on 14.10.2016 at about 12.10 pm, Near Village Dulhera, Haryana,
regarding which DD bearing No. 32/2016 was registered at PS Jhajjar.

The offending vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. HR-76B-9182, which at the time of accident was being driven by respondent No. 1 (R-1), owned by respondent No. 2 (R-2) and insured with respondent No. 3 (R-3).
2.

Succinctly put, facts of the case as per claim petition are that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the petitioner along with his four colleagues were going from Bahadurgarh to Jhajjar in vehicle bearing registration No. HR-76B- 9182, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at high speed and in rash and negligent manner.

When they reached near village Dulheda, all of a sudden, a cow came on the road and in the process of avoiding collision with the cow, the vehicle turned turtle due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

It is further stated that the petitioner was initially removed to Oscar Hospital and thereafter, he was shifted to Balaji Action Medical Institute,

sentences.text: Respondent no. 1 and 2 have filed their joint written statement wherein it is stated that the respondent no. 1 was holding a valid driving license and the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of alleged accident.

Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company has filed its written statement wherein it is stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with them in the name of respondent no. 2 w.e.f. 03.02.2016 to 02.02.2017, however, the liability of Insurance Company is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is further stated that the alleged vehicle was being driven by a person without holding a valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was used contrary to the terms and conditions of RC, fitness and insurance policy.

5. On 07.11.2017, the following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court :-
1.

Whether the injured Ishan Qazi sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 14.10.2016 at about 12.10 pm, near Village Dulhera, Haryana caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. HR-76B-9182 driven by respondent No. 1 and owned by respondent No. 2 and insured with respondent No. 3?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

3. Relief.
6.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined total four witnesses, including himself as PW1.
However, no evidence in rebuttal came on record from any of the respondents.

7. The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh.
Ravi Qazi, Ld. Counsel for petitioner, Sh. Sunil Kumar, Ld. Counsel for R1 and R2 and Sh.
Dwapayan Gupta, Ld. Counsel for R- 3/Insurance Company.
The case record as well as written submissions filed on behalf of parties have also been carefully perused.
The finding on the aforesaid issues is reproduced in succeeding paragraphs hereinafter.

1. Whether the injured Ishan Qazi sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 14.10.2016 at about 12.10 pm, near Village Dulhera, Haryana caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
HR-76B- 9182 driven by respondent No. 1 and owned by respondent No. 2 and insured with respondent No.
3?

OPP. 
8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
In order to prove negligence of respondent No. 1, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1.

He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ishan Qazi vs Jatin Yadav on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162823724/
2 Ex. PW-1/A, wherein he has narrated the mode and manner of accident as well as the injuries sustained by him and treatment taken thereafter.
The petitioner has tendered on record attested copy of complaint bearing DD No. 32 dated 15.10.2016 as Ex. PW1/7 (colly) in respect of the accident, which had occurred a day before.

PW1 also placed on record his MLC prepared at Advanta Super Specialty Hospital, Jhajjar, Haryana as Ex. PW1/2, showing the alleged history of RTA (car accident) on 14.10.2016 at 12.15 am lodged at PS Sadar, Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, Haryana.

sentences.text: 9. During cross examination, he deposed that there were five persons in their vehicle, including driver and they all were studying in the same college located at Bahadurgarh.
He further deposed that no quarrel took place between any of them either in the car or prior to boarding the car.
He further deposed that the car belonged to Jatin as he used to bring it in the college, however, he (PW1) was not aware in whose name it was registered.
He further deposed that he had been wearing the safety belt at the time of accident and was sitting on the back seat of the car.
He denied the suggestion that the accident did not occur due to rash and negligent driving of Jatin.
He further denied the suggestion that Jatin was driving the said car with controlled speed or that the accident had taken place only due to the fact that a cow had suddenly jumped infront of the car.

10. The petitioner has also examined one Sh. Sajjan Kumar, previously working as ASI in PS Sadar Bahadurgarh, District Jhajjar, Haryana as PW3, who deposed that on 15.10.2016, he received an intimation about a road accident near Village Dulhera and visited the place of accident.

He further deposed that on 14.10.2016 at 11 pm, HC Jitender from PS Jhajjar had informed him on his telephone that 2-3 young boys met with an accident near Village Dulhera and they were admitted in Advanta & Oscar Hospital at Jhajjar.

Thereafter, he reached there and found one Jatin, who told him that he along with his friends Sachin, Ishan, Skanlap and Ankit were going to Jhajjar in the car of his uncle Sanjay, having registration No. HR-76B-9182.

He further deposed that Jatin was driving the car and when they reached near Village Dulhera, suddenly, a cow came infront of their car and they met with an accident when in order to save the cow, their car turned turtle.
He further deposed that Ishan, Sachin and Skanlp had sustained injuries.
He further deposed that he did not record the statement of Ishan as the doctors declared him unfit for making statement whereas Sachin, Skanlap and Ankit had given their statements.
Thereafter, he collected the MLCs of all the injured persons from the hospital authorities and also took the photographs of accidental car after reaching at the spot of accident.
He has placed on record photocopy of DD entry bearing No. 32 dated 15.10.2016 as Ex. PW3/A (colly). During cross examination
, he deposed that no statement of eye witness was recorded in the present matter.

11. The victim/injured i.e. the petitioner herein, being one of the passenger in the offending vehicle,
had himself witnessed the accident.
As per his testimony, his friend Jatin, who was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident, had been rash and negligent as he was driving it at high speed.

Besides putting bald suggestion to deny rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle, nothing material could be elicited to rebut the testimony of said witness in this regard.
It is an admitted case of defence (R1) that car turned turtle when a cow suddenly jumped onto the road.
However, had the speed of car been slow, the accident could have been avoided.
Further, an animal like a cow is big enough to be visible from a distance and the driver could have slowed down the vehicle, had the vehicle been driven at a controlled speed.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an Accident Tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in case titled as Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
14.

In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no.
HR-76B-9182 which was being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 at the relevant time of accident.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner(s) is/are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

15. As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the petitioner, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;

4 (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

17. Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.

In his affidavit Ex.PW1/A, the petitioner has tendered on record his discharge summary as Ex.
PW1/2 (colly), as per which the petitioner was admitted in Balaji Action Medical Institute, Paschim Vihar, New Delhi on 15.10.2016 and was discharged on 31.10.2016.

sentences.text: It further reflects that the petitioner was diagnosed with RTA with head injury-DAI, fracture nasal bone and had undergone nasal bone fracture reduction with CLW repair with dressing of stitched wound B/L arm and forearm.
19. The petitioner in his affidavit has also tendered on record his original medical bills as Ex. PW1/6 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 4,27,611/-.
During cross examination, he admitted that he has not filed on record prescriptions of the doctors.

He volunteered that the medicines which have been prescribed in Ex. PW1/2 were the initial medicines prescribed by the doctor, but subsequently,
the medicines kept on changing as per the doctor's prescriptions.
He further admitted that the prescriptions by which the doctor has changed the medicines, has not been filed on record.

20. The petitioner has examined one Sh. Ravinder Kumar, Record Incharge from Advanta Super Specialty Hospital, Jhajjar, Haryana as PW2 who has placed on record copy of admission record of petitioner as Ex. PW2/1, copy of discharge record as Ex. PW2/2 and copy of bill issued by their hospital as Ex. PW2/3 (colly).

21. On the other hand, the respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.

Thus,
the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.4,27,611/- towards his medical expenses.

sentences.text: It is evident from the testimony of PW4 coupled with the aforesaid exhibited documents that the petitioner was matriculate, however, he was pursuing his BCA course at the time of accident and due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he remained absent in all the classes from 2nd semester till 6th semester.
The fact that the petitioner remained absent in his college from 2nd to 6th semester, goes to show that he was unable to resume his routine work for almost two and half year.
25. Since the income of the petitioner has not been established on record, the minimum wages of matriculates is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Haryana.
As per the petitioner's own case, he was studying in Haryana and even the Adhar card of petitioner placed on record shows his address of Haryana.
Accordingly, the minimum wages prevalent in the State of Haryana shall be applicable, which was Rs. 342.21/- per day at the time of accident.

Hence, the income of deceased comes out to be Rs. 8,897/- (rounded off) (Rs.342.21 X 26 days).
26.

Keeping in view the duration of his treatment and nature of injury suffered by him and the fact that he could not attend his college for almost two and half year, this tribunal finds it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 30 months.

Therefore,
under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.2,66,910/- (Rs.8,897/- X 30 months).
(iii) Loss of future earnings 27.

As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital, the petitioner was examined there by the medical board and after his examination, the doctors have opined that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical or mental impairment.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled to any amount under this head.
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 28.
As is reflected from the discharge summary and photographs of petitioner on record, the petitioner had suffered multiple grievous injuries on his head, face and arms in the accident.

sentences.text: Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.
Further, an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,25,000/- under this head.

(v) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 29. PW1 in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that he had spent an amount of Rs.50,000/-
towards conveyance and Rs. 35,000/- on special diet.
However, he has not placed on record any document in order to substantiate his above claims.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for frequently visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with long treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Accordingly, an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance and Rs. 25,000/- towards special diet.
30. The petitioner in his affidavit has claimed that he was confined to bed for a period of more than 10 months due to which he had engaged one attendant for 24 hours @ Rs. 15,000/- per month.
However, he has not placed on record any document to show that he had engaged any attendant for his day to day activities.

Still keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, he would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work for atleast 12 months, therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month for 12 months is also being awarded to the petitioner towards attendant charges.
The claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.1,95,000/- (Rs.50,000/- + Rs.25,000/- + Rs. 10,000/- X 12 months) under this head.
(vi) Disfigurement 31.
As already discussed above, the petitioner had sustained fracture injuries on his nose and had undergone some surgeries on his face which has caused incision marks on his face.
32. In view thereof, the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for disfigurement of his face.
Accordingly, considering the marks of injuries sustained by the petitioner on his face and head, the petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
(vii) Loss of prospects of marriage 33.
The petitioner in his affidavit has claimed that he was 20 years old and unmarried at the time of accident.

(viii) Loss of education 35.
As already noted above, on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner could not attend his college from second semester till the end of 6th Semester.
In this regard, petitioner has examined PW4 who has proved on record certificate issued by PD Memorial College of Engineering as Ex. PW4/C.

As per cross examination of PW4, the petitioner was absent in all the classes from second semester till 6th semester.
36. In the light of above facts and circumstances, a lump- sum amount of Rs.2,50,000/- is also being awarded to the petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The offending vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. HR-76B-9182, which at the time of accident was being driven by respondent No. 1 (R-1), owned by respondent No. 2 (R-2) and insured with respondent No. 3 (R-3).
2.
When they reached near village Dulheda, all of a sudden, a cow came on the road and in the process of avoiding collision with the cow, the vehicle turned turtle due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
4. Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company has filed its written statement wherein it is stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with them in the name of respondent no. 2 w.e.f. 03.02.2016 to 02.02.2017, however, the liability of Insurance Company is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
In order to prove negligence of respondent No. 1, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the injured Ishan Qazi sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 14.10.2016 at about 12.10 pm, near Village Dulhera, Haryana caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. HR-76B-9182 driven by respondent No. 1 and owned by respondent No. 2 and insured with respondent No. 3?
OPP.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is an admitted case of defence (R1) that car turned turtle when a cow suddenly jumped onto the road.
Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an Accident Tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
16. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
It is evident from the testimony of PW4 coupled with the aforesaid exhibited documents that the petitioner was matriculate, however, he was pursuing his BCA course at the time of accident and due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he remained absent in all the classes from 2nd semester till 6th semester.
The fact that the petitioner remained absent in his college from 2nd to 6th semester, goes to show that he was unable to resume his routine work for almost two and half year.
25. Since the income of the petitioner has not been established on record, the minimum wages of matriculates is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Haryana.
As per the petitioner's own case, he was studying in Haryana and even the Adhar card of petitioner placed on record shows his address of Haryana.
Accordingly, the minimum wages prevalent in the State of Haryana shall be applicable, which was Rs. 342.21/- per day at the time of accident.
Keeping in view the duration of his treatment and nature of injury suffered by him and the fact that he could not attend his college for almost two and half year, this tribunal finds it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 30 months.
As per disability certificate issued by Dr. RML Hospital, the petitioner was examined there by the medical board and after his examination, the doctors have opined that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical or mental impairment.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled to any amount under this head.
(iv) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 28.
As is reflected from the discharge summary and photographs of petitioner on record, the petitioner had suffered multiple grievous injuries on his head, face and arms in the accident.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.
